name: The fourteen root downfalls
description: Breaches that destroy the tantric pledge — despising the master, anger at vajra kin, abandoning bodhicitta, revealing secrets, disparaging women and the rest; with them there is no attainment and one falls to hell.
antidotes: renewal of the vows by consecration (Advayavajra: 'take bodhicitta and the vows again before the guru in the maṇḍala')

name: The gross downfalls
description: Secondary breaches of the tantric vow, listed after the root downfalls in the Advayavajrasaṃgraha.

name: Practising without consecration
description: Taking up tantric practice without the precious consecration: like a blind man stealing the king's treasury or an outcaste hoping to be king; punished by the ḍākinīs.

name: Unconventional conduct before realization
description: Engaging in the observance without realization: 'like a kingdom seized by its subjects' (Nāgārjuna's song); base conduct after realization likewise degrades.

name: Hope and fear
description: The poison of hope and fear intoxicates the yogin's mind and binds the innate gnosis; the fruit manifests only without them.

name: Pride in powers and practices
description: Pride in forceful yogic techniques or attainments ('out of pride they call themselves yogins'); pride obscures the wish-fulfilling jewel of non-conception.
antidotes: not clinging to one's own realization (Dhūmapa)

name: Clinging to meditative experiences
description: Taking experiences — dream-bliss, the moments and joys, the bliss of the aggregates — for the ultimate, 'brass for gold'; realization without experience, or experience clung to, both fall short.

name: Distraction
description: A distracted mind does not realize reality; the jewel is lost in the thicket of things; 'without distraction is the king of meditations'.

name: Conceptual thought (vikalpa) as the adverse side
description: Conceptual thought (rnam rtog) is the enemy destroyed by the siddhas' realization — the deer of grasped and grasper shot by Śavaripa, the adverse side torn by Līlapa's ten perfections, the waves stilled by seeing one's mind.

name: The three poisons
description: U44 contribution: desire, hatred and delusion — which the Vajrayāna transforms into the gnoses (the smith 'forges the three poisons into the dharmakāya'; the nature of anger is the nature of mind).
